prose.text: Keep the bottom copy of Z. Collapse the whole top copy to one point.
Collapse the top copy of Z
Drag either shape to rotate both · arrow keys also rotate.
The top is 100% of its original width. The identification happens at 1. The cone on a filled disk is a solid cone, homeomorphic to a 3-ball.
A cylinder keeps a separate copy of Z at every height. The cone identifies every point at height 1 to the same apex. This is a quotient construction.
For a circle base, there are no filled caps: the cylinder and cone here are surfaces. Choosing a filled disk includes every interior point and produces a solid cylinder or solid cone.
The intermediate pictures show how the top approaches the identification. Here Cone(Z) names a space; C(A) in the other views names an assigned carrier region.
Carrier proof · pp. 21–22 · Cones · Hatcher, Chapter 0
